page: Amazon Web Services r5d.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 2400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 209.41 GB/sec and large-block write memory bandwidth at 92.36 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent tier. Multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 54167.75 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11070.0. Conversely, single-core capabilities are weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25 percent tier. Large-model LLM prompt processing performs at an average level, though text generation speeds are weak.

The primary tradeoff of the r5d.16xlarge lies in its high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage versus its lower single-threaded compute efficiency. This profile makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that require rapid local scratch space but do not depend on high single-core CPU clock speeds. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, and memory-heavy data processing tasks.
